newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai may defer rule on Arabic food labels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dubai may defer rule on Arabic food labels - paper.

text.p: Dubai may defer a requirement for food importers to use Arabic labels on their products, Monday's Gulf News quoted an official as saying.
Dubai, one of the seven emirates of the United Arab Emirates, announced in March it would implement the regulation from July 22.

"The regulation on Arabic labelling of food products will be discussed in a meeting by the general secretariat of the United Arab Emirates municipalities," Qassem Sultan, Director General of Dubai Municipality, was quoted as saying.
"We will reconsider the matter because it is difficult for our traders to force factories to Arabise labels on food products, especially ingredients," the newspaper quoted him as saying.

He said the decision to defer implementation of the regulation was taken after supermarkets and traders expressed concern that the move could lead to price hikes and the disappearance of products from store shelves.
Sultan did not set a new date for implementing the regulation.

Abdul-Rahman al-Mutaiwee, Director General of Dubai's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, had said importers and manufacturers of packaged food products should comply with Arabic labelling or face the risk of a ban on their imports.
Traders in Dubai said that 40 to 50 percent of the products now on the market do not comply with the Arabic labelling regulation.
